item.title: Representation theory and massive spectral zeta functions on spherical space forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.05490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the spectral theory of the massive scalar kinetic operator on spherical space forms $\Gamma \backslash S^{3}$, where $\Gamma$ is a finite subgroup of $\mathrm{SO}(4)$ acting freely on $S^{3}$. Using the Peter-Weyl theorem and Molien series we compute the spectrum of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on $\Gamma\backslash S^3$ directly from representation theory, obtaining the eigenvalues and their multiplicities for all lens spaces $L(p,q)$ and for each ADE-class of finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, which includes homogeneous lens spaces, prism spaces and quotients by the binary tetrahedral, octahedral and icosahedral groups, the last also known as the Poincar\'e homology sphere. For homogeneous quotients by subgroups of even order, we construct the meromorphic continuation of the spectral zeta function of the massive kinetic operator and obtain the general zeta-regularized determinant in closed form. The determinant is expressed as a finite sum of polylogarithms, valid for all real mass, and depends on $\Gamma$ only through its order and a finite set of parameters which we call twist coefficients fixed by the dimensions of the $\Gamma$-invariant subspaces. As a complementary approach, we express the heat trace of the kinetic operator on spherical space forms in terms of Jacobi theta functions, whose modular properties relate the spectral zeta function to geometric data, the volume and closed geodesic lengths of $\Gamma\backslash S^3$. We find that the spectral zeta function admits a rapidly convergent expansion in the heavy mass sector in terms of modified Bessel functions, and provides an independent check on the determinant. This framework extends to quotients of higher-dimensional manifolds directly, which we outline for future work.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Martin, Allan Merino, Rahul Poddar, Simon Roby

item.title: Rough-to-frozen transition in non-integrable dimer models
item.description: arXiv:2611.05516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The transition from rough to frozen phases in models of random surfaces is expected to be governed by the Pokrovsky-Talapov law, which predicts a $\varepsilon^{3/2}$-type singularity of the macroscopic height profile (limit shape), as the distance $\varepsilon$ from the frozen phase (facet) is sent to zero. This has been proved so far only in exactly solvable cases, notably the classical, determinantal, 2D dimer model. In this paper we prove the validity of the Pokrovsky-Talapov law for a non-integrable 2D dimer model on the hexagonal lattice, whose Gibbs weight depends upon a weak plaquette interaction among dimers. Our proof is based on a multiscale analysis (constructive fermionic Renormalization Group), which allows us to identify two different regimes with distinct scaling properties and to explain the universality of the Pokrovsky-Talapov exponent $3/2$, in contrast with the interaction-dependent critical exponents characterizing the rough phase. The first regime, corresponding to smaller distances, is characterized by an effective quadratic dispersion relation, while the second comes with an effective linear dispersion relation, typical of Luttinger liquid behavior. As a byproduct of our construction, we control the scaling limit of the interacting dimer model uniformly in the distance from the frozen phase.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Giuliani, Vieri Mastropietro, Bruno Renzi, Fabio Toninelli

item.title: Stroh--Hamiltonian Framework for Modeling Incompressible Poroelastic Materials
item.description: arXiv:2611.05554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Stroh sextic formalism, developed by Stroh, offers a compelling framework for representing the equilibrium equations in anisotropic elasticity. This approach has proven particularly effective for studying multilayered structures and time-harmonic problems, owing to its ability to seamlessly integrate physical constraints into the analysis. By recognizing that the Stroh formalism aligns with the canonical Hamiltonian structure, this work extends its application to Biot's poroelasticity, focusing on scenarios where the solid material is incompressible and there is no fluid pressure gradient. The study introduces a novel Hamiltonian-based approach to analyze such systems, offering deeper insights into the interplay between solid incompressibility and fluid-solid coupling. A key novelty lies in the derivation of canonical equations under these constraints, enabling clearer interpretations of reversible poroelastic behavior. However, the framework assumes perfectly drained conditions and neglects dissipative effects, which limits its applicability to fully realistic scenarios involving energy loss or complex fluid dynamics. Despite this limitation, the work provides a foundational step toward understanding constrained poroelastic systems and paves the way for future extensions to more general cases, including dissipative and nonlinear regimes.
item.dc:creator: Kinza Arshad, Vincenzo Tibullo

item.title: When light travels with infinite speed: the electromagnetic loop circuits
item.description: arXiv:2611.05606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Considering the ideal limit where the speed of light is infinite, or more precisely where the permittivity and permeability of the vaccuum are both zero, we construct a new type of electromagnetic circuit that we name an EM-loop circuit. These consist of wires having very high permittivity (E-wires) and wires having very high permeability (M-wires). These are threaded together by coils, the E-wire loops and M-wire loops. Some of the loops are terminal loops, pierced by an applied magnetic flux (for E-wire loops) or an applied displacement field (for M-wire loops) that are outside the vacuum since it does not support these fields. The response is the net flux of displacement field through a cross section of each E-wire terminal loop and the net magnetic flux through a cross section of each terminal M-wire loop. To calculate this response, the fields at the internal loops (those that are not terminal loops) are eliminated from the equations.It turns out that the response is governed by a new class of function pairs - dual Herglotz functions. Superpositions of a special class of EM-loop circuits, termed fundamental, allow us to realize any pair of dual Herglotz functions. Thus, we have obtained a complete characterization of the response functions of EM-loop circuits.
item.dc:creator: Graeme W Milton, Pierre Seppecher

item.title: A liquid vapor phase transition in quantum statistical mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2611.05641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a liquid vapor phase transition for a quantum system of particles in the continuum. The system is the quantum version with Boltzmann statistics of the point particles model introduced in by Lebowitz, Mazel and Presutti.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Baffioni, Tobias Kuna, Immacolata Merola, Errico Presutti

item.title: Dynamical Signatures of Selective Gap Closing in Multi-Dimensional Monotone Quasiperiodic Operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.05686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We translate the spectral gap-closing criterion for multi-dimensional monotone quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators into a concrete dynamical protocol and verify it by large-scale numerics. For a non-principal label we construct a sampling function whose leading eigenfunction weight at the origin vanishes; a local bump then drives the residual weight through zero. The height of a weighted oscillatory time average of the origin-to-localization-center correlator exhibits a deep minimum precisely at the closing, while the site-control label remains featureless and orders of magnitude larger. The signature is robust and maps directly onto superconducting-circuit and photonic platforms.
item.dc:creator: Leonid Parnovski, Roman Shterenberg

item.title: Compatible Condensation and Generalized Gauging: Marked Transport and Wall Interchange
item.description: arXiv:2611.06104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate condensation compatible with a specified separable generalized gauging operation in a unitary (2 + 1)-dimensional defect realization. Compatibility is a coherent reversible crossing of the full condensate algebra, retaining charged channels and the marked condensation interface. The resulting composite network determines the transported condensate, the induced operation, and a commuting square of specified walls. For connected gauging data, compatibility admits a central matching description that retains the transported condensate and its algebra identification on the specified wall. The specified unit may absorb a nontrivial parent anyon algebra; strong connectedness appears only as the transparent-unit specialization. We distinguish original vacuum insertions, vacuum branches after unit absorption, and the full vacuum algebra of the final phase, and we prove a complete Higgs criterion that incorporates the parent algebra absorbed by the specified unit. In the toric-code example of a non-invertible subgroup gauging we classify the compatible condensations for the fixed operation, exhibit two inequivalent crossings of the same parent condensate that lead to different final phases, and analyse a pure condensation operation in which the specified unit absorbs the parent electric condensate and produces additional final vacuum operators. The transparent-unit case recovers reverse-condensation transport and the vacuum-overlap formula, and the three complete Higgs conditions appear as a corollary of the general criterion.
item.dc:creator: Youxuan Wang

item.title: The Quantum Stochastic Limit for Non-Markovian Driving Processes
item.description: arXiv:2611.06202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We express the stochastic limit (weak-coupling limit) of a quantum system interacting with its environment as the limit of solutions to a parametrized family of quantum stochastic differential equations (QSDEs). We prove the convergence of such solutions in the case where the driving processes may be non-Markovian and the system may be infinite-dimensional with unbounded Hamiltonian. We achieve this by imposing a particular condition on the n-point functions of the driving process which we verify for annihilation, creation, and gauge operators on a bosonic Fock space with sufficient mixing. Additionally, we include not only the usual fast-evolving system Hamiltonian which is averaged out in the limit, but also a slow-evolving system Hamiltonian which survives the limit. We also relax the requirement for the fast-evolving Hamiltonian to have a purely discrete spectrum allowing accumulation points under some circumstances. Moreover, our convergence mode for the processes is convergence of all time-centered n-point functions which is stronger than the typical semigroup convergence for the stochastic limit.
item.dc:creator: Tanner J. Reese

item.title: Fluctuating Hydrodynamics of Quantum Fluids from the Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.06485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Starting from the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation (NFPE), we establish the fluctuating hydrodynamics for quantum fluids. We also investigate the corresponding stochastic thermodynamics and derive the associated fluctuation theorems. We then apply this framework to both fermionic and bosonic systems. For the ideal Fermi gas, we study the electrical conduction and reveal a resistance proportional to the product of temperature and the density of states at the Fermi surface. For bosonic fluids, we analyze the relaxation time characterizing the critical slowing down phenomenon and identify three distinct scaling behaviors corresponding to the non-interacting, repulsive interaction, and attractive interaction regimes. Overall, this work provides a experimentally verifiable phenomenological description for the dynamics of quantum fluids and demonstrates the applicability of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation in characterizing such systems.
item.dc:creator: Mingjian Gu, Zhaoyu Fei, Xiaoguang Wang

item.title: Spectral properties of twisted soft waveguides
item.description: arXiv:2611.06558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss a model of a soft waveguide described by Schr\"{o}dinger operator whose potential is a twisted straight channel of non-circular profile. We show that a compactly supported twist makes the operator subcritical, the property being expressed in terms of a Hardy-type inequality. On the other hand, a periodic twist raises the essential spectrum and its local slowdown may give rise to isolated eigenvalues below the essential spectrum threshold.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Exner, David Spitzkopf

item.title: A Counterexample to the Weak Gibbs and Regularity Conjectures
item.description: arXiv:2611.06617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a counterexample to the weak Gibbs and regularity conjectures. The example is a spin-one system on the square lattice with a translation-invariant nearest-neighbor interaction. At high temperatures and high on-site field strengths, it has a unique KMS state that does not have the weak Gibbs or regularity properties.
item.dc:creator: Marius Wesle

item.title: Large particle number asymptotics for point-interacting bosons in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.06669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider $N$ bosons in two dimensions interacting via point interactions, modeled by the TMS Hamiltonian. We prove that their ground state energy has the asymptotic behavior $-e^{C N }$ for large $N$, for an explicit constant $C$ related to the sharp constant in the Ladyzhenskaya-Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality. Such asymptotic behavior was predicted in the physics literature, based on a variant of the mean-field approximation.
item.dc:creator: Rupert L. Frank, Robert Seiringer

item.title: Concavity of Normalized Generalized Br\'ezin--Gross--Witten Correlators and Its Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.06675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the generalized Br\'ezin--Gross--Witten model using its BKP integrability. By virtue of the formula for connected $n$-point functions of tau-functions of the BKP hierarchy obtained by Wang and the first-named author, we prove that the normalized generalized BGW correlators are strictly concave for fixed genus and fixed total degree. As applications, we establish the strict Schur-concavity and derive upper and lower bounds for these correlators. We also prove the strict monotonicity of normalized ordinary BGW correlators, which resolves a conjecture by Guo--Norbury--Yang--Zagier.
item.dc:creator: Chenglang Yang, Xuhui Zhang

item.title: A local Yang-Baxter obstruction for the hard-square model
item.description: arXiv:2611.06780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many exact solutions of two-dimensional lattice models rest on an analytic family of weights satisfying the Yang-Baxter equation. The hard-hexagon model was solved in this way, while the neighbouring hard-square model has no known closed form. We determine the height alphabets that encode hard squares without hidden heights, and there are exactly two connected ones, the occupation variables themselves and the four heights of Andrews, Baxter and Forrester. Hard hexagons is integrable on both, but no analytic Yang-Baxter family of face weights passes through hard squares at nonzero activity on either. The difference lies in the exclusion rule, which for hard squares turns a few Yang-Baxter equations into polynomial identities that force auxiliary weights to vanish. A closed form for hard squares is not excluded, but a solution by this route would have to leave these encodings or go beyond a single analytic family through the model. Encodings with hidden heights remain open.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Ortega, Eliecer Pe\~na-Ancavil

item.title: Spectral measures and sharpness of quantum speed limits
item.description: arXiv:2611.05462v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum speed limits bound the time required for a given state to evolve into a given subspace of the Hilbert space under specific energy constraints. We prove that for several standard orthogonalization time bounds, the unique spectral measure associated with the initial vector that saturates the bound is a sum of two Dirac measures. Furthermore, we constrain the families of spectral measures that come arbitrarily close to these bounds and construct examples with measures which are purely absolutely continuous and purely singular continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure. As a complementary perspective, we discuss the geometric intuition behind quantum speed limits provided by the numerical range of the evolution operator.
item.dc:creator: Ivica Smoli\'c

item.title: Raychaudhuri-Ehlers Kinematics on Quantum State-Space: Caustics and Extrinsic Quantum Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.05499v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum mechanics is inherently geometric in that the pure states form a curved complex manifold and the Schr\"odinger evolution defines a Hamiltonian flow on this space. Geometry identifies constraints on flows on quantum state-space that hold independently of their microscopic realization. We uncover such universal behavior in families of geodesic paths on the quantum state-space using the Raychaudhuri-Ehlers equations. We show that the complex structure leads to tidal anisotropy in the curvature, and for Hilbert space dimension $N\geq3$, complete point-emitted geodesic bundles necessarily develop shear and undergo direction-selective focusing at finite distance. We give these geometric results an information-theoretic interpretation in terms of fidelity susceptibility and quantum Fisher information. For ground-state manifolds constrained by physical parameters, we resolve the tidal curvature into Berry-curvature-dependent ambient tides and contributions from extrinsic bending within the full ambient state space. We further relate extrinsic bending to variations in the unitary generator of motion along intrinsic geodesics. We present exact many-body geometric results for the transverse-field XY spin chain. The product structure of the ground state leads to an exact cancellation of the ambient tide, including its Berry-curvature enhancement, by extrinsic curvature contributions. At the zero-field Ising point, we obtain exact results at finite size and show that the shear source for anisotropy-directed motion is entirely extrinsic relative to the full many-body state-space. For the metric in the thermodynamic limit, the geodesic families exhibit repeated $A_2$ fold catastrophes inside the ferromagnetic phase. Our framework thus separates universal state-space effects from those of physical restrictions and exposes their consequences in a paradigmatic many-body system.
item.dc:creator: Neellohit Karmakar, Suraj S. Hegde, Aryan Bhatia

item.title: Chiral edge modes from lattice Chern-Simons theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.05663v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is shown that a level $k$ Abelian lattice Chern-Simons theory with continuum time and a spatial square lattice, which is a topological field theory on the latticized plane and torus, when quantized on a spatial cylinder reduces to chiral edge excitations, exactly localized on the two boundaries and carrying two commuting lattice versions of the level-$k$ $U(1)$ Kac-Moody algebra of opposite chirality. The algebras are represented on a Fock space in the noncompact theory and by a finite Weyl algebra in the compact one. We also observe that the theory has a natural framing of Wilson loops which exhibits the correct framing anomaly.
item.dc:creator: Gordon W. Semenoff

item.title: Discovering like a scientist: Literature-informed dimensionless learning for physical closure of data-driven equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.05780v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data-driven methods can recover compact equations, yet the physical dependence of their coefficients across operating conditions often remains unresolved. Dimensionless groups can explain this variation, but selecting relevant groups from the many dimensionally admissible combinations remains challenging. Here, we introduce a knowledge-guided framework for dimensionless learning, called {\pi}-former. It learns patterns of variable association and exponent assignment from a corpus of 1,288 established dimensionless groups. Under exact dimensional constraints, the model proposes interpretable basic groups whose combinations are optimized against observations. Across seven physical problems, the framework identifies predictive dimensionless coordinates within seconds. Integration with equation discovery further expresses condition-dependent coefficients through these coordinates, recovering established physical scalings in multi-condition simulations. Applied to experimental measurements of evaporation-driven wetting, the framework discovers dimensionless coordinates and uses them to construct a unified trajectory equation. The resulting model generalizes to held-out conditions across liquids and initial volumes, outperforming existing empirical models. These results establish dimensionless learning as a transferable bridge between accumulated scientific knowledge and data-driven equation discovery, enabling artificial intelligence to uncover physically meaningful laws from observations.
item.dc:creator: Hao Xu, Tianhao Wu, Dongxiao Zhang

item.title: Near linear mixing of random-cluster Glauber dynamics on random regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.05794v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the random-cluster model on locally treelike graphs at low temperatures. This is a model of dependent percolation parametrized by an edge probability $p \in (0,1)$ and a clustering weight $q \in [1,\infty)$, generalizing independent Bernoulli percolation ($q=1$) and closely related to the classical ferromagnetic Ising and Potts spin systems at integer $q$. For $q>2$, at parameter $p$ below the tree uniqueness threshold $p_{\mathsf u}(q,d)$, it is expected that sampling is easy and local Markov chains mix rapidly on all graphs with degree bounded by $d$. On typical graphs, the same is predicted at $p>p_{\mathsf s}(q,d)$, where $p_{\mathsf s}(q,d)$ is a second uniqueness transition point on the $d$-regular wired tree. Our result confirms this prediction for random regular graphs, showing that the random-cluster Glauber dynamics mix in time $O(n^{1+o(1)})$ on a random $d$-regular graph for all fixed $q>2$ and $p>p_{\mathsf s}$. For comparison, the best prior sampling results for these models that held for all $p>p_{\mathsf s}$ required $q\gtrsim \log d$ \cite{BGPZ26}. The key difficulty is that simply utilizing the contraction of cavity messages on $d$-regular trees does not suffice to cover the entire regime $q>2$. To address this issue, motivated by \cite{LS26}, we develop a careful bootstrap argument to show the shrinkage of disagreement under grand coupling. The core ideas of the proof were generated using GPT-6 and the Pharos system; the proof was then refined and simplified by the author.
item.dc:creator: Zhangsong Li

item.title: Gaussian free field limit for the Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble
item.description: arXiv:2611.05852v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the centered height function of the Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble converges for each $\beta>0$, under rescaling of space and time variables, towards the Gaussian free field in the half-plane. The conformal structure for GFF involves the spatial change of coordinate $x\mapsto \sqrt{-x}$. The $\beta$--dependence is isolated in the field rescaling by $\sqrt{\beta}$. For the proofs we study the asymptotic expansions of the moments of Laplace transforms of the Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble developed in our previous work with Xu.
item.dc:creator: Vadim Gorin, Lingfu Zhang

item.title: BMV conjecture and positivity of spectral shift for relatively Schatten perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2611.05879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish BMV-type results and prove the positivity-preserving property and uniqueness of support-normalized spectral shift functions of arbitrary order for semibounded operators with relatively Schatten-von Neumann perturbations. We also derive correlation inequalities in the relative Hilbert-Schmidt case. These results build on a new positivity-preserving property for the trace of a higher-order operator derivative along a relatively Schatten direction and are obtained using methods of multilinear operator integration and approximation.
item.dc:creator: Chandan Pradhan, Anna Skripka

item.title: Frequency-Frame Covariance for Reactive-Power Scalarization
item.description: arXiv:2611.05913v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Measured voltage and current waveforms may be represented in a reference frame whose frequency differs from the physical fundamental frequency. Reactive-power readouts calculated from such frequency-shifted coordinates may change if their readout operators are not transformed consistently. This paper presents a frequency-frame covariance formulation for finite-spectrum, zero-mean periodic waveforms with complete harmonic information over one physical period. A necessary and sufficient covariance condition is derived, requiring the readout operator to transform consistently with the waveform representation. Consequently, frequency-dependent harmonic weights must be evaluated at physical harmonic orders rather than relative frame labels. In particular, the derivative/Iliovici readout equals a relative-derivative contribution plus an explicit reference contribution. The formulation also separates readout-operator errors from errors caused by changes in the physical components retained by waveform projections. Three analytical cases illustrate conditional carrier recovery for a memoryless resistor, physical-frequency weighting at relative zero in an RLC branch, and the possibility that an exact reactive-power scalar can coexist with a substantial waveform error after projection. The scope is deterministic calculation consistency in frequency-shifted coordinates rather than instrument measurement uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Kai Sun

item.title: Toward Shifted symplectic Chiralization: Deformation of Courant Algebroids
item.description: arXiv:2611.06031v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the chiralization of Poisson--Lie theory through graded symplectic geometry. We compare Courant deformations and classical $r$- and $R$-matrix constructions, obtaining integrable hierarchies and free field realizations. We give a variational description of the obstruction to Lie conformal bialgebra compatibility and recover Liberati's obstruction in the Virasoro case. We also introduce a vertex bialgebra analogue of quantized universal enveloping algebras and construct explicit quantizations to all orders of Cartan type Lie conformal bialgebra structures on $\operatorname{Cur}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$. These results contribute to the first author's broader programme of developing shifted symplectic chiralization as a geometric method for constructing chiral analogues of Poisson-Lie structures via $n$-shifted symplectic geometry, and exploring its connections with AKSZ theory and quantization.
item.dc:creator: Wenda Fang, Noriaki Ikeda

item.title: Discrete Backbone Elasticity and Curvature-Dependent Torsion Statistics in Proteins
item.description: arXiv:2611.06363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coarse-grained models of protein conformational dynamics use $\mathrm{C}_\alpha$ geometry to describe the probabilities of regular helices, ordered turns and disordered conformations. To test how much of this order arises from local chain elasticity, we connect discrete Hasimoto frame transport to neighboring bending mismatch, deriving a curvature-product torsion interaction and a six-parameter generalized von Mises density. Fitted on 194 chains from the ATLAS molecular dynamics database and tested on 1744 sequence-nonredundant proteins, this baseline reduces negative log-density loss from 1.490 to 1.160 nats, torsion-sign error from 12.26 to 2.15 percentage points, and helix-fraction error from 21.84 to 10.41 points. Ablations and circular-moment projections against reference generative models motivate extensions to anisotropic stiffness and two partition-function-weighted elastic states, further lowering test loss to 0.790 nats and helix error to 1.65 points. The fixed hierarchy also improves predictions across 72 trajectories of peptides $\mathrm{Fs}$ and $(\mathrm{AAQAA})_3$ and miniprotein $\mathrm{HP35}$ spanning varied starting conformations and force fields. Remaining angular errors in these trajectories are associated with atomic context at shared bends, as bend-matched peptide frames adopt opposite torsion signs with distinct hydrogen-bond patterns and a proline-containing $\mathrm{HP35}$ turn remains at negative torsion. Introducing a bilinearly coupled $\mathrm{C}_\alpha$--$\mathrm{N}$ orientation angle largely reparameterizes the existing bend-dependent harmonics, with an empirical $L^2$ Gram projection placing 96.7\% to 99.6\% of its added coefficient-function squared norm within the original six-function span. These results link discrete Hasimoto elasticity to statistical backbone potentials and clarify the scope and limits of local $\mathrm{C}_\alpha$ geometry.
item.dc:creator: Yiquan Wang, Mingyu Bian, Jiayuan Ma

item.title: Higher Integrability, Generalized Symmetries, and Partially Topological Field Theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.06507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We exhibit a classical link between higher Lax integrability and generalized symmetries in a non-Lorentzian higher semi-holomorphic Chern--Simons theory on $M\times\mathbb CP^1$. The equations of motion determine a spectrally dependent flat higher connection on $M$ whose Laurent coefficients organise an infinite hierarchy of conserved quantities. We construct a spectral family of classical $(d_M-2)$-form symmetry line defects associated with the Lax connection, establish an action-preserving deformation law, and exhibit suitable gauge-invariant probes on which the induced transformations act nontrivially.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Alfonsi, Leron Borsten, Mehran Jalali Farahani, Hyungrok Kim, Martin Wolf, Charles A. S. Young

item.title: Stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter
item.description: arXiv:2611.06528v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In quantum many-body physics and quantum field theory, it is often assumed that gapped systems remain gapped under sufficiently weak local perturbations. However, to what extent this assumption holds is elusive, except for some special systems. In this work, we examine the stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter that is only subject to two physically natural conditions, locality and translation invariance. We first show that in any spatial dimension, there are gapped local Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap, i.e., they become gapless under certain arbitrarily weak local perturbation in the thermodynamic limit. We then prove that for both spin and fermionic systems in one dimension, such Hamiltonians with an unstable gap must not only break translation invariance but also be fine-tuned. We further show that in any dimension greater than one, there are fine-tuned local translation invariant Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap. These results greatly sharpen our understanding of the fundamental problem of the stability of quantum phases of matter. We also discuss implications of our results on, for example, anyon superconductivity and higher-form symmetries.
item.dc:creator: Kangle Li, Liujun Zou

item.title: The super Weil-Petersson asymptotic expansion and the coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.06621v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the universal constant in the large-genus asymptotic expansion of super Weil-Petersson volumes. The argument adopts the uniform-transport strategy for shifted theta intersection numbers. The uniform large-genus theorem for normalized BGW numbers of Guo-Norbury-Yang-Zagier determines the amplitude at a simpler endpoint. The result is $C=\pi^{-9/2}$. We give a proof of the Griguolo-Papalini-Russo-Seminara conjecture for fixed boundary lengths and fixed descendant degrees. The boundary formula is uniform when the sum of the lengths is $o(\sqrt g)$, and we exhibit an obstruction at the $\sqrt g$ scale. We also compute the first four inverse-genus coefficients by two exact recursive methods and derive general polynomial structure results. Finally, we show that, for each fixed genus, the super Weil-Petersson volume divided by $n!$ is a polynomial in the number $n$ of marked points.
item.dc:creator: Xuanyu Huang, Kefeng Liu, Hao Xu

item.title: On isospectral potentials on periodic discrete graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider discrete Schr\"odinger operators with periodic (possibly complex valued) potentials $Q$ on periodic graphs. Using a system of spectral invariants obtained in \cite{S26}, we investigate the sets of isospectral potentials on periodic graphs. In particular, we show that the Floquet spectrum of the Schr\"odinger operators on the hexagonal lattice and on the Kagome lattice generically (with respect to perturbations of $Q$) determines the potential $Q$ uniquely up to the obvious symmetries (translations and rotations) in the periodic graph.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Saburova

item.title: Heavy-Light Wall Crossings and Motivic Asymptotics of Moduli Spaces of Curves. Part I: Stabilization Graphs and Euler Characteristics
item.description: arXiv:2611.06862v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we develop an explicit calculation of ordinary topological Euler characteristics of the coarse moduli spaces underlying Hassett spaces in the minimal all-light chamber and the Deligne-Mumford compactification. For genus $g\ge2$, we organize the calculation through a decomposition indexed by stabilization graphs and their decorations. The Burnside-Lefschetz formula allows us to compute the resulting contributions, taking into account graph symmetries and their fixed loci. The calculation in genus two illustrates the method explicitly and, in the Deligne-Mumford case, recovers the generating function of G. Bini, G. Gaiffi, and M. Polito (arXiv:math/9806048), with the corrections of G. Bini and J. Harer (arXiv:math/0506083), providing a check on the construction. We also carry out the calculation in genus three in an appendix. Together with an elementary genus-one calculation based on collision partitions and rational necklaces, these formulas yield complete asymptotic expansions as the number of labeled markings tends to infinity. The passage from all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics is governed by the universal change of variables $\Phi(z)=(2-z)e^z-2$, which we derive by a direct wall-crossing argument. For arbitrary fixed genus $g\ge2$, the same framework identifies the leading contribution of rational trivalent graphs and gives the ordinary asymptotic scale $n!(e-2)^{-n}n^{(3g-5)/2}$. The leading constants are the symmetry weights of these graphs; we derive their generating function, recurrence, and large-genus behavior. We also determine the asymptotic ratio of all-light to ordinary Euler characteristics, answering a question of S. Kannan, S. Serpente, and C. H. Yun (arXiv:2207.02800).
item.dc:creator: Giordano Cotti

item.title: Conformal field theory from automorphic forms on a quantum group
item.description: arXiv:2611.06907v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We reformulate two-dimensional conformal field theory (2d CFT) in the language of noncommutative geometry. To this end, we introduce automorphic forms for the von Neumann algebraic quantum group $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. A quantum measure space is a von Neumann algebra equipped with a weight. We study such spaces carrying a weight-preserving action of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. We argue that every unitary bosonic 2d CFT with central charge $c=1+6(b+b^{-1})^2>1$ is equivalent to a quantum measure space with an action of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})\times\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. In this dictionary, Virasoro primary operators are quantum automorphic forms and their scaling dimensions correspond to the spectrum of a quantum Laplace operator. The Virasoro crossing equations express associativity of multiplication on the quantum measure space. For compact theories, the algebra is a type III$_1$ factor. Liouville CFT is realized as $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$ acting on itself by left and right translations. Virasoro boundary conditions correspond to quantum measure spaces with an action of a single copy of $\mathrm{SL}^+_b(2,\mathbb{R})$. When the boundary spectrum is discrete, these are noncommutative counterparts of compact hyperbolic surfaces. The formulation accommodates models both with and without extended chiral algebras. It bridges the Virasoro conformal bootstrap with categorical and von Neumann algebraic approaches to 2d CFT.
item.dc:creator: Dalimil Mazac

item.title: Using topology to reveal all mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
item.description: arXiv:2611.06917v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) describe complementary quantum measurements: certainty in one basis gives no information about the others. In dimension six, triples of MUBs are known, but whether a fourth basis could exist remained unresolved for over three decades. OpenAI recently reported a proof that none exists. Here we use the topology of the space of complex Hadamard matrices, which describe transitions between MUBs, to characterize all sets in dimension six. We prove that every mutually unbiased triple belongs to a two-parameter family or is a single isolated triple built from the Fourier matrix. Since none of them extend to a fourth basis, this also proves that no four MUBs exist. Our proof rests on a new topological result that all order-six complex Hadamard matrices except Tao's form a connected space. Connectedness reduces the classification of triples to finitely many overlapping four-dimensional phase balls. We certify with interval arithmetic that these balls cover the space and for every pair of MUBs represented in a ball, we then determine all third bases that extend it. Dimension six is now the first non-prime-power dimension in which all sets of MUBs are classified.
item.dc:creator: Mateo C\'ardenes Wuttig, Joseph Tindall

item.title: The Spear and the Ring: Emergent Structures in Magnetic Colloidal Suspensions
item.description: arXiv:2504.02379v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study from a mathematical point of view the nanoparticle model of a magnetic colloid, presented by G. Klughertz. Our objective is to obtain properties of stable stationary structures that arise in the long-time limit for the magnetic nanoparticles dynamics following this model. In this article, we present a detailed study of two specific structures using techniques from the calculus of variations. The first, called the spear, consists of a chain of aligned particles interacting via a Lennard-Jones potential. We establish existence and uniqueness results, derive bounds on the distances between neighboring particles, and provide a sharp asymptotic description as the number of particles tends to infinity. The second structure, the ring, features particles uniformly distributed along a circle. We prove its existence and uniqueness and derive an explicit formula for its radius.
item.dc:creator: Rapha\"el C\^ote (IRMA, USIAS), Cl\'ementine Court\`es (IRMA, MACARON), Guillaume Ferriere (Paradyse), Ludovic Godard-Cadillac (UB, IMB, Bordeaux INP), Yannick Privat (IECL, SPHINX, IUF)

item.title: Antiferromagnetic Long-Range Order in a Lattice Fermion Model
item.description: arXiv:2508.12421v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a lattice fermion model with antiferromagnetic interactions on the three-dimensional cubic lattice. The hopping term of the Hamiltonian has a Weyl-type dispersion. We prove that the model has reflection positivity. Moreover, by relying on the property, we prove the existence of the antiferromagnetic long-range order at low temperatures in a strong coupling regime.
item.dc:creator: Yukimi Goto, Tohru Koma

item.title: Semiclassical resonances under local magnetic fields
item.description: arXiv:2604.17854v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study resonances for the semiclassical magnetic Laplacian in the full plane with a compactly supported magnetic field in the framework of semiclassical complex scaling and black box scattering theory. Assuming that the magnetic field is locally constant, we prove the existence of semiclassical resonances near the Landau levels with exponentially small imaginary parts. We also prove that resonances emerge from a magnetic step discontinuity along a curved interface or a non-degenerate magnetic well, and in the vicinity of anharmonic Landau levels if the field has an isolated zero.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Exner, Ayman Kachmar

item.title: Strong-disorder expansion of the root-averaged density of states for the Anderson model on the Bethe lattice
item.description: arXiv:2605.00478v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the root-averaged density of states for the Anderson model on the Bethe lattice in the strong-disorder regime. Here the density of states means the root-averaged spectral measure, not a finite-volume eigenvalue counting limit. We assume that the single-site distribution has compact support and has a locally analytic density on an interval $I^\sharp$ containing a given interval $I$. Combining the random-walk expansion on the tree with a complex-analytic argument for the single-site Stieltjes transforms, we prove that the scaled averaged diagonal resolvent has a holomorphic continuation to a complex neighborhood of $I$ for all sufficiently large $\lambda$. By the Stieltjes inversion formula, the root-averaged density of states measure is absolutely continuous on the scaled energy window $\lambda I$, and its density is real analytic and has a finite-order strong-disorder expansion there. In the scaled form $E=\lambda\xi$, the leading coefficient is the local density of the single-site distribution. All odd coefficients vanish, and the higher coefficients are finite sums determined by occupation profiles of short closed walks on the tree. For the uniform single-site distribution, we compute the first nonzero correction term explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Masahiro Kaminaga

item.title: Quantum estimates for classical polynomial optimization
item.description: arXiv:2607.25445v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The problem of finding lower and upper bounds on multivariate homogeneous polynomials is both difficult and important given its applications to questions ranging from dynamical stability in complex potential landscapes to data analysis. From the standpoint of tensor eigenvalue theory, the question is equivalent to finding the smallest and the largest eigenvalues of the coefficient tensor corresponding to the given polynomial. Standard approaches outlined in the literature amount to running nonlinear iterations in search for the optimal rays along which the growth of the polynomial is fastest or slowest. Unlike the case of matrices (or their corresponding multivariate quadratic forms) convergence of such algorithms for higher-rank tensors is capricious due to the complex topography of polynomial objective functions. In this essay, a very different strategy, inspired by quantum-mechanical variational methods, is introduced for finding bounds on polynomials. The original polynomial is replaced by an operator acting in a suitably chosen (large) space of states, such that in an appropriate "classical" limit this operator approaches the original polynomial expression made of commutative variables. As a result, approximating the smallest and largest eigenvalues of the coefficient tensor, and thus finding bounds on polynomials, amounts to diagonalizing the resulting quantum operator, represented as a large matrix, and then inspecting the smallest and largest eigenvalues of this matrix. This approach is then successfully applied to standard test examples from tensor eigenvalue literature and other problems of interest in mathematical physics including Strichartz-type inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Evnin

item.title: Gaussian $\beta$-Markov Path Spaces without a Spectral Gap and the Araki--Woods Representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.34783v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Derezi\'nski and G\'erard constructed the Gaussian $\beta$-Markov path space of a free Bose field in a form equivalent to the Araki--Woods representation, which suits nonequilibrium statistical mechanics with a quantum-field environment, but only for one-particle Hamiltonians with a spectral gap. We extend this construction, together with the equivalence to the Araki--Woods representation, to one-particle Hamiltonians without a spectral gap. For one-particle Hamiltonians joined by isometric embeddings that intertwine their spectral measures and test spaces, as for nested momentum lattices, and for compatible regularizers, the path spaces form a projective system whose limit carries the time translations and the reflection, which gives a quasi-local construction. The extension is intended for constructive quantum field theory at positive temperature and equilibrium statistical mechanics, for instance in the problem of the absence of Bose--Einstein condensation of quasiparticles whose number is not conserved.
item.dc:creator: Yoshitsugu Sekine

item.title: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits
item.description: arXiv:2610.40235v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the three-dimensional chiral $\Z_p$ Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun--Yang--Wang--Tantivasadakarn--Chen are, for every odd prime $p$, not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such statements were known only inside the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. The key ingredient is a new invariant of invertible subalgebras, which we conjecture to be the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory, modulo rational squares.
item.dc:creator: Bowen Yang

item.title: Comments on flavor symmetry breaking and three-dimensional superconformal index
item.description: arXiv:2303.00482v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the superconformal index of a three-dimensional $SU(2)$ ${\mathcal N}=2$ supersymmetric QCD with $N_f=4$ flavors. This theory confines with the breaking of a global symmetry. We obtain the index of this theory by integrating out a flavor from the theory with $N_f=6$ flavors. The superconformal index of the theory vanishes for generic values of the flavor fugacities. However, the specific choice of fugacities allows us to describe the flavor symmetry-breaking phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Ilmar Gahramanov

item.title: Foundations on k-contact geometry
item.description: arXiv:2409.11001v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: $k$-Contact geometry is a generalisation of contact geometry to analyse field theories. As a main goal, we develop an approach to $k$-contact geometry based on distributions that are distributionally maximally non-integrable and admit, locally, $k$ commuting supplementary Lie symmetries: the $k$-contact distributions. More specifically, we investigate the existence of Reeb vector fields for $k$-contact distributions, $k$-contact Lie groups are defined and studied, and, after analysing compact manifolds, a Weinstein conjecture for a product of $k$ compact contact manifolds is discussed. Polarisations for $k$-contact distributions are introduced and it is shown that a polarised $k$-contact distribution is locally diffeomorphic to the Cartan distribution of the first-order jet bundle over a fibre bundle of rank $k$. We relate $k$-contact manifolds to presymplectic and $k$-symplectic manifolds on fibre bundles of larger dimension and define types of submanifolds in $k$-contact geometry. We study Hamilton--De Donder--Weyl equations on $k$-contact Lie groups. A theory of $k$-contact Hamiltonian vector fields is developed, and we describe characteristics of Lie symmetries for first-order partial differential equations in a $k$-contact Hamiltonian manner. We use our techniques to analyse Hamilton--Jacobi and Dirac equations, types of Engel and Goursat distributions, physical problems, and control systems. The work also presents introductory results so as to make it more self-contained.
item.dc:creator: Javier de Lucas, Xavier Rivas, Tomasz Sobczak

item.title: A direct algebraic proof for the non-positivity of Liouvillian spectral values and controlling the dissipative gap of unital systems
item.description: arXiv:2504.02256v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Markovian open quantum systems are described by the Lindblad master equation $\partial_t\rho =\mathcal{L}(\rho)$, where $\rho$ denotes the system's density operator and $\mathcal{L}$ the Liouville super-operator, which is also known as the Liouvillian. For systems with a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, it is a fundamental property of the Liouvillian that the real parts of all its eigenvalues are non-positive. Analogously, for infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, the Liouvillian as a map on trace-class operators only has spectral values with non-positive real parts. The usual arguments for these properties are indirect, using that $\mathcal{L}$ generates a quantum channel and that quantum channels are contractive. We provide a direct algebraic proof based on the Lindblad form of Liouvillians. Subtleties for infinite-dimensional systems are highlighted. For example, unbounded operators can then be eigenvectors of the adjoint Liouvillian with positive eigenvalues, corresponding to a physical instability of the system. As an illustrative application of the algebraic approach, we prove that a strict minimum can be imposed on the dissipative gap of any unital Markovian spin-$s$ or fermionic many-particle system by adding simple local dissipators. The added dissipators comprise Pauli or generalized Pauli Lindblad operators for spin systems and Majorana Lindblad operators for fermionic systems.
item.dc:creator: Yikang Zhang, Thomas Barthel

item.title: Variational formulae for entropy-like functionals for states in von Neumann algebras
item.description: arXiv:2510.07605v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The paper presents variational formulae for entropy-like functionals, including Segal and R\'enyi entropies, for normal states on semifinite von Neumann algebras. The considered functionals are of the form $\tau(f(h))$ where $\tau$ is a normal faithful semifinite trace on this algebra, $h$ is a positive selfadjoint operator from $L^1(\mathscr{M},\tau)$, and $f$ is an appropriate convex or concave function. The results cover both finite and semifinite algebras, and the obtained formulae generalise known results, in particular, those concerning relative entropy. Moreover, the connection between quantum entropies and the structure of abelian subalgebras is highlighted, providing new interpretations in the context of quantum information theory.
item.dc:creator: Andrzej {\L}uczak, Hanna Pods\k{e}dkowska, Rafa{\l} Wieczorek

item.title: Landau Hamiltonian with Gaussian white noise potential and the asymptotics of the bottom of its spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2511.22162v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a simple construction of a random Schr\"odinger operator subject to a magnetic field with a regularity as low as $0^-$-H\"older and a Gaussian white noise electric potential on a two-dimensional bounded box. This construction is based on the exponential Ansatz introduced in [HL15] and leverages the semigroup approach developed in [HL24]. The proposed construction enables us to generalise an asymptotic result for the bottom of the spectrum of the two-dimensional continuous Anderson Hamiltonian, first proved in [CvZ21], to the magnetic case. Our choice of potential not only covers the case of a uniform magnetic field, but also those which would break translational invariance.
item.dc:creator: Yueh-Sheng Hsu

item.title: Dirac solitons in one-dimensional nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2512.24089v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we study a family of one-dimensional stationary cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger (NLS) equations with periodic potentials and linear part displaying Dirac points in the dispersion relation. By introducing a suitable periodic perturbation, one can open a spectral gap around the Dirac-point energy. This allows to construct standing waves of the NLS equation whose leading-order profile is a modulation of Bloch waves by means of the components of a spinor solving an appropriate cubic nonlinear Dirac (NLD) equation. We refer to these solutions as Dirac solitons. Our analysis thus provides a rigorous justification for the use of the NLD equation as an effective model for the original NLS equation.
item.dc:creator: William Borrelli, Elena Danesi, Simone Dovetta, Lorenzo Tentarelli

item.title: On integrals of non-autonomous dynamical systems in finite characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2602.09298v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use a difference Lax form to construct simultaneous integrals of motion of the fourth Painlev\'e equation and the difference second Painlev\'e equation over fields with finite characteristic $p>0$. For $p\neq 3$, we show that the integrals can be normalised to be completely invariant under the corresponding extended affine Weyl group action. We show that components of reducible fibres of integrals correspond to reductions to Riccatti equations. We further describe a method to construct non-rational algebraic solutions in a given positive characteristic. We also discuss a projective reduction of the integrals.
item.dc:creator: Nalini Joshi, Pieter Roffelsen

item.title: Clustering without geometry in sparse networks with independent edges
item.description: arXiv:2603.13159v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The coexistence of sparsity and clustering (non-vanishing average fraction of triangles per node) is one of the few structural features that, irrespective of finer details, are ubiquitously observed across large real-world networks. This fact calls for generic models producing sparse clustered graphs. Earlier results suggested that sparse random graphs with independent edges fail to reproduce clustering, unless edge probabilities are assumed to depend on underlying metric distances that, thanks to the triangle inequality, naturally favour triadic closure. This observation has opened a debate on whether clustering implies (latent) geometry in real-world networks. Alternatively, recent models of higher-order networks can replicate clustering by abandoning edge independence. In this paper, we mathematically prove, and numerically confirm, that a sparse random graph with independent edges, recently identified in the context of network renormalization as an invariant model under node aggregation, produces finite clustering without any geometric or higher-order constraint. The underlying mechanism is an infinite-mean node fitness, which also implies a power-law degree distribution. Further, as a novel phenomenon that we characterize rigorously, we observe the breakdown of self-averaging of various network properties. Therefore, as an alternative to geometry or higher-order dependencies, node aggregation invariance emerges as a basic route to realistic network properties.
item.dc:creator: Alessio Catanzaro, Remco van der Hofstad, Diego Garlaschelli

item.title: Chewing gums, snakes and candle cakes
item.description: arXiv:2605.12572v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The aim of these lecture notes, based on lectures given by the second author at the CIME school in Cetraro, is to illustrate a range of ideas surrounding higher Teichmuller spaces of Riemann surfaces with marked boundaries through explicit and computationally tractable examples. After reviewing the classical Teichmuller space of hyperbolic Riemann surfaces with boundary and its combinatorial description in terms of Thurston shear coordinates on a fat-graph, we explain how the bordered cusped Teichmuller space arises as a confluent limit when two boundary components in the Riemann surface collide via the so-called chewing-gum move giving rise to a candle cake. We then revisit these constructions from the Fock-Goncharov perspective, explaining snake calculus for transport matrices in PSL_n(R) and explain how the chewing gum move is the inverse of amalgamation. Rather than focusing on formal proofs, our goal is to illustrate the underlying theorems and constructions in a concrete and intuitive way.
item.dc:creator: Benedetta Facciotti, Marta Mazzocco, Nikita Nikolaev

item.title: Interference Queueing Networks: A Replica Mean-Field Approach in the Symmetric Setting
item.description: arXiv:2606.13264v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a model for evaluating the performance of wireless communication networks beyond the ubiquitous full-buffer assumption, under which every transmitter is always active. The network is represented by N interacting queues arranged on a torus, with homogeneous arrival rate and service rates depending on the activity of neighboring interferers. More precisely, each queue is associated with a transmitter-receiver pair, and its service rate is given by the Shannon capacity, which depends on the corresponding Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR). Since interfering transmitters only emit when their queue is non-empty, the SINR, and hence the service rate, improves when neighboring queues are empty. We first derive the stability region of the system. To investigate the stationary regime, we introduce two mean-field approximations. The first one is obtained from a finite K-replica system, for which we prove propagation of chaos as K goes to infinity. The second one describes a queueing system evolving in a suitably chosen environment. We derive quantitative estimates comparing these two approximations. Finally, we prove that the original interacting queueing system converges exponentially fast to stationarity.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Sarotte, Nahuel Soprano-Loto, Fran\c{c}ois Baccelli

item.title: S$^{2}$-PINN: Stochastic Separable Physics-Informed Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.03303v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Uncertainty quantification (UQ) for random partial differential equations (PDEs) is ubiquitous in computational science and engineering. However, classical spectral solvers for this class of problems face the curse of dimensionality, and existing neural solvers often ignore the stochastic structure that makes moments and calibration tractable. We introduce a stochastic separable physics-informed neural network, dubbed S$^{2}$-PINN, that represents the solution $u(t,\mathbf{x},\mathbf{Z})$ of a random PDE with a learnable Gaussian spatial dictionary, Fourier temporal features, and a generalized polynomial chaos (gPC) stochastic basis, coupled by a low-rank Canonical Polyadic (CP) tensor decomposition core. The method is trained with a hybrid strong-form and gPC-projected residual loss. Our theoretical analysis establishes that the separable class is dense in $L^2$ under mild conditions, and the projected residual corresponds exactly to a stochastic Galerkin constraint. Furthermore, we show that mini-batch projection coefficients are logarithmically dependent on the number of gPC modes, and that the orthogonality penalty controls the conditioning of the learned spatial dictionary. Using four manufactured random PDE benchmarks, we show that S$^{2}$-PINN outperforms nine baselines in terms of mean and variance accuracy, as well as calibration, while using significantly fewer parameters. Further evaluations on non-manufactured Poisson and Darcy problems, a stochastic Navier--Stokes problem, a diffusion scaling study of higher random dimensions, and two stochastic inverse problems reveal the generalization capabilities of the proposed structure. Together, these results support stochastic separability as an effective design principle for physics-informed neural UQ. The code for the experiments can be found in https://github.com/DMax1314/s2pinn
item.dc:creator: Zhendong Li, Akwum Onwunta

item.title: Compact toric Einstein four-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.10425v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This is a continuation of our previous paper on toric gravitational instantons. We develop a systematic theory of compact simply-connected Einstein four-manifolds with toric symmetry. Applications include (1) The construction of simply-connected positive Einstein four-manifolds with arbitrarily large $b_2$. Our method is based on local gluing combined with a global virtual counting argument. The key idea involves a particular design of rod structures to enable a gluing construction and restrict possible degenerations. (2) A topological characterization of algebraically special toric Einstein metrics in terms of $b^+_2 \leq1$. This uses special curvature identities for $W^+$ in the toric setting. (3) Uniqueness, up to scaling and isometry, of toric Einstein metrics on four-manifolds admitting an algebraically special Einstein metric. (4) Diffeomorphism classification of compact toric Einstein four-manifolds in terms of an improved Hitchin-Thorpe inequality $\chi\geq3|\tau|$. (5) Smooth compactness of simply connected toric Einstein four-manifolds with bounded Euler number. In particular, our construction recovers all the classical toric Einstein metrics, including the Page and Chen-LeBrun-Weber metrics, starting from the round sphere through moduli spaces of conical Einstein metrics.
item.dc:creator: Mingyang Li, Song Sun

item.title: Global well-posedness and long-time asymptotics for the focusing coupled Kundu--Eckhaus equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.16564v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove global well-posedness in the Schwartz space and establish long-time asymptotics for the focusing coupled Kundu--Eckhaus (CKE) equation. For data with no discrete spectrum or real-axis spectral singularities, we analyze the associated matrix Riemann--Hilbert problem by the Deift--Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method. A quantitative local expansion of the full matrix factor near the stationary point identifies the unitary factor in the leading vector term. We combine an estimate for the full matrix coefficient at infinity with exact mass identities. This gives joint error estimates for the gauge-equivalent coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger solution, the cumulative mass, and the gauge phase. These joint estimates yield an explicit asymptotic formula for CKE radiation with an $O(t^{-1}\log t)$ remainder, uniformly for $x/t$ in compact subsets of $\mathbb R$. We also compute the reflection coefficient and the unitary endpoint factor to visualize the asymptotic solution.
item.dc:creator: Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang

item.title: A self-organizing mechanism for collective foraging: recruitment cascades couple Levy search to a clustered maximum-entropy resource field
item.description: arXiv:2610.24865v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Foraging recruitment is modeled as a contagion: an agent that finds a resource triggers a linear-threshold cascade on the group's communication network. Because activation is degree-normalized, crowding shuts the cascade off, so the swarm aggregates on a resource and then disperses to explore again. Acting on the cascade moves agents in space, and that motion rewires the network, so recruitment and exploration are one coupled process; removing this coupling alone abolishes the self-limitation. Recruitment spreads only within a connectivity window, bounded below by percolation onset and above by degree-blocking. The swarm self-organizes to the near-critical edge of this window -- self-organized quasi-criticality: recruitment sits near but below the critical point without settling onto a clean, size-invariant critical state, and the activity spectrum has a finite correlation time (Lorentzian-like, not 1/f), consistent with local rather than global criticality. Recruitment raises harvest up to 2.7x over solitary search on sparse, clustered resource fields and loses (down to 0.37x) on abundant or uniform ones; because resources generically aggregate, the favourable regime is the common one. The empirically motivated Levy search and the resource field it exploits are both least-committal: the search a maximum-caliber walk, and the field a maximum-entropy point process whose generic, aggregation-set sign is clustered (attractive). The search exponent that maximizes harvest tracks the field's fractal dimension (a heavier-tailed, more ballistic search for more strongly clustered fields). These are one coupled mechanism: heavy-tailed Levy exploration crosses the field's sparse voids while recruitment cascades exploit its clusters, so one maximum-entropy geometry binds exploration and recruitment into a single self-organizing cycle.
item.dc:creator: Galen J. Wilkerson

item.title: Superregular solitonic solutions of the defocusing nonlocal nonlinear Schrodinger equation and their novel perspectives
item.description: arXiv:2610.33560v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Previous studies have indicated that the local defocusing nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation (NLSE) is modulationally stable. Therefore, superregular solitonic solutions characterizing the nonlinear evolution of modulational instability under weak localized perturbations do not exist. In this work, we study the nonlinear stage of the modulation instability of a condensate in the framework of the defocusing nonlocal NLSE. By using the dressing method and Joukowski transformation, we systematically derive the general $N$-solitonic solution of the defocusing nonlocal NLSE, and the explicit expressions for one-solitonic, two-solitonic and superregular two-solitonic solutions are provided. Then dynamics of these solutions is also examined. We find that these solutions show a much wider variety than those in the local NLSE, such as the one solitonic solution composed of two interacting wave components and the two-solitonic solution containing four wave components. Finally, the accuracy and noise robustness of the analytical solutions are confirmed by numerical simulations. Such results advance the theory of superregular solitonic solutions in nonlocal systems and offer new physical understanding of wave propagation in nonlocal nonlinear media.
item.dc:creator: Duan-Yun Xia, Xiu-Bin Wang

item.title: Bubble Tree Convergence for Minimisers of a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.37457v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study degree $1$ minimisers $u: (\Sigma,g) \to S^2$ for a Baby-Skyrme model with a Sacks-Uhlenbeck regularisation term $E^{\alpha}(u) = \frac{1}{2} \int_{\Sigma} (1+\vert \nabla u \vert^2)^{\alpha+1} -1 dv_g$ and establish convergence of degree $1$ minimisers to a simple bubble tree as $\alpha \to 0$. We also obtain a new no-neck result for the classical Sacks-Uhlenbeck energy $E^{\alpha}$.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Woodward

item.title: Lojasiewicz Estimates for a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.37499v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the structure of degree $1$ minimisers of a Baby-Skyrme energy of maps $u:\Sigma \to S^2$ regularised by a Sacks-Uhlenbeck perturbation, and we establish quantitative convergence rates to a simple bubble tree consisting of a single degree $1$ bubble and a constant base map.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Woodward

item.title: Analytic Solutions To Fully Quantized Parametric Amplification
item.description: arXiv:2610.39387v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive analytic expressions for observable dynamics under the fully quantized trilinear Hamiltonian, governing quantum three-wave mixing and parametric amplification. Starting from a coherent pump and vacuum signal and idler, the calculation reorganizes the Heisenberg expansion into resummed depletion and return profiles, yielding directly evaluable expressions for all 1st-, 2nd- and 3rd-order correlations. The construction uses no parametric approximation or fitted parameters. Representative numerical benchmarks show errors of order $10^{-12}$ throughout the entire pump depletion, and below $10^{-3}$ across dozens of depletion-and-back-conversion cycles, up to the first total collapse of the oscillation. The first-depletion treatment additionally provides 4th-order correlations, accommodates bright squeezed-pump inputs and reveals phenomena important to future optical quantum technologies. The framework can be extended to higher moments.
item.dc:creator: Wanli Xing, Timothy C. Ralph

item.title: Linking-form splitting and four-dimensional genera of knots
item.description: arXiv:2610.40183v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: By Gilmer's splitting lemma, the linking form of a rational homology sphere that bounds a 4-manifold is the orthogonal sum of a metabolic summand and a summand presented by a form of the rank of the intersection form. The lemma underlies Gilmer's slice genus theorem and the rank criteria of Murakami-Yasuhara and Gilmer-Livingston for nonorientable surfaces and the 4-dimensional clasp number. We show that the lemma and these results, as stated, are false. For each prime $p \equiv 3 \pmod 8$ we construct knots bounding smooth M\"obius bands, and knots bounding smooth punctured tori with clasp number one, whose linking forms have no such summand of rank at most two. We then determine what remains true: the lemma holds up to Witt equivalence and for cube-free orders, and its conclusions about summands hold away from exceptional primes and for orientable surfaces of genus at least two. Finally, we find the optimal Witt-class bound for the topological nonorientable 4-genus.
item.dc:creator: Seong-Jin Lee

item.title: Tracy-Widom law for sample covariance matrices under quadratic form concentration
item.description: arXiv:2610.41416v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study sample covariance matrices formed from vectors $q_i = \Sigma^{1/2}u_i \in \mathbb{R}^M$, $1 \leq i \leq N$, where $u_1, \ldots, u_N$ are independent, centered, isotropic random vectors whose coordinates may not be independent. We assume that the random vectors $q_i$ satisfy a concentration bound for their quadratic forms $q_i^T A q_i$. Under this assumption and a regular right edge condition on $\Sigma$, we establish edge universality and obtain the Tracy-Widom law for the largest eigenvalue of the sample covariance matrix after appropriate centering and scaling. In particular, for log-concave ensembles, our result removes the unconditionality assumption imposed in existing edge universality results~\cite{BX}, resolving the question that originally motivated our work. The concentration assumption also allows us to extend the result beyond the log-concave class.
item.dc:creator: Guangchen Chen, Xing Lyu
